defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: netrc_auth.py:17 expanduser prepends ~/ to the NETRC value, breaking absolute paths
netrc_auth.py:12 empty NETRC string treated as valid path, resolves to $HOME directory
test only uses relative NETRC, never absolute path
votes.evidence_quote: `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` prepends `~/` to every entry in `netrc_locations`, including the value from `NETRC`. When `NETRC` is an absolute path like `/etc/netrc`, this produces `~//etc/netrc` which expands to `$HOME//etc/netrc`, a non-existent path.
votes.justification: The review points to the expanduser call in get_netrc_auth. It explains that an absolute NETRC path gets the ~/ prefix and resolves under $HOME, so no credentials are found. That is the known defect.
